category: duplicate network protocol and persisted-state authority
title: The live core network reader silently drops rerun metadata written by the desktop coordinator
observed_behavior: The desktop coordinator's network protocol and registry persist rerun-aware fields, while separately maintained core copies omit them. Desktop InFlightJob writes job_kind and claim_metadata; core InFlightJob.from_dict ignores both. The core application facade then loads coordinator_inflight.json through that stale core registry. A no-write round trip proved that core ClaimResponse drops eleven desktop fields, core DoneRequest drops twelve, and core InFlightJob drops job_kind plus claim_metadata.
expected_invariant: One canonical network wire/state contract must own every field, and every supported reader of coordinator_inflight.json or claim/done payloads must preserve fields it does not reinterpret, especially rerun identity and handoff evidence.
root_cause: Network protocol, registry-support, persistence, and facade implementations were copied into both core/network and desktop/network and are still independently live. Rerun/network additions landed in the desktop writer/transport tree without an enforced parity or migration path for the core reader tree.
failure_scenario: A coordinator persists a rerun claim with job_kind=rerun and claim_metadata containing batch/row identity. The worker-board or rerun projection reads the same file through the core registry, silently erases those fields during deserialization, and can present incomplete recovery evidence or make later state handling indistinguishable from an ordinary pipeline-queue claim. Future maintenance can also update one ClaimResponse/DoneRequest copy while the other remains wire-incompatible.
evidence: desktop/network/registry_support.py lines 194-195 and 211-233 serialize and restore job_kind and claim_metadata; core/network/registry_support.py lines 169-213 has no corresponding fields.

core/network/registry_persistence.py line 101 constructs the stale core InFlightJob from every persisted in-flight job, and core/network/facade.py lines 623-640 uses that registry for the operator worker projection.
desktop/network/protocol.py adds eleven ClaimResponse fields and twelve DoneRequest fields absent from core/network/protocol.py; the current coordinator HTTP handler imports the desktop protocol.

The no-write round-trip reproduction retained every field through desktop classes but reported desktop-only ClaimResponse fields coordinator_source_path, destination_policy_applied, handoff_probe, job_kind, output_handoff, planned_output_path, rerun_batch_id, rerun_row_index, rerun_row_key, source_identity, worker_source_path; DoneRequest additionally lost worker_result_artifact_path.

The protocol and registry-support pairs have different current SHA-256 hashes, while several neighboring network modules remain byte-identical, confirming an actively diverged copy family rather than a historical archive.
affected_flows: rerun results queue projection and operator evidence
existing_safeguards: The active desktop coordinator/worker protocol and registry have extensive direct tests, including network rerun claims and persistence/recovery.
Registry loading is fail-closed for malformed JSON and uses bounded normalization for known fields.
The core facade reports a warning when coordinator state cannot be loaded at all.
safeguard_gap: Those safeguards validate the desktop writer/reader pair or total-load failure. They do not compare the core copy, preserve unknown fields, or flag successful-but-lossy core deserialization; no direct test imports core.network.protocol.
tests_present: tests/python/desktop/test_network_protocol_runtime.py exercises the desktop protocol and registry runtime.
tests/python/desktop/test_network_rerun_claims.py exercises rerun-aware desktop claims and registry state.
tests_missing: Cross-tree schema/parity test for core and desktop ClaimResponse, DoneRequest, and InFlightJob.
Core-facade test loading a desktop-written rerun coordinator_inflight.json and asserting job_kind/claim_metadata survive into the projection.
Migration or unknown-field-preservation test for persisted network state.
recommended_remediation: Choose one canonical network protocol/registry authority and import it from both application layers. Migrate the core worker-board/rerun readers to the desktop writer's current persisted contract (or move that contract into a neutral core/contracts package), preserve unknown fields during any transition, and delete the redundant copies only after import/package compatibility is proven. Add exact field-set and desktop-write/core-read round-trip tests.
remediation_risk: High: coordinator claims, persisted recovery state, and network lifecycle are high-risk surfaces. Consolidation must preserve existing JSON, old-worker compatibility, path identity, auth boundaries, and operator recovery evidence.
validation_rung: Targeted network protocol, registry persistence/recovery, rerun-network, application-facade worker-board, and rerun projection tests; strict Local API network lifecycle tests; synthetic coordinator write/core read round trips. Representative real-media validation is not required for the contract consolidation itself.
prior_audit_relationship: No current finding ledger contained either network protocol path or this lossy dual-reader root cause; this is a new current-hash finding.

title: Duplicated encoder maps disagree on h264_amf and the capability fallback rejects a supported codec
observed_behavior: The wizard and wizard-tools encoder-name maps recognize h264_amf as H.264, but encoding_capabilities._ENCODER_CODECS_BY_NAME omits it. When a valid available descriptor row has encoder_name=h264_amf and lacks a usable family field, the capability-row fallback advertises the AMF backend but no H.264 codec. The same encoder-name input through the wizard advertises both. A supported h264_amf preset then receives a video.codecFamily unsupported-capability issue.
expected_invariant: All supported encoder names must resolve through one canonical descriptor/name policy, and equivalent discovered encoder evidence must produce the same codec-family and backend facts in settings validation and the wizard.
root_cause: Three manually maintained encoder-name maps encode overlapping policy. h264_amf was added to the wizard copies and accepted option policy but not to the capability-row fallback copy; tests cover descriptor rows only when family is already populated.
failure_scenario: A capability probe or imported descriptor supplies an available h264_amf row without a recognized family value. Settings/preset validation reports that H.264 is unavailable even though the wizard and option schema expose h264_amf and the backend fact correctly reports AMF. An operator can be blocked from saving or using an otherwise supported encoder configuration.
evidence: settings_wizard.py and settings_wizard_tools.py line 88 map h264_amf to h264; encoding_capabilities.py lines 19-31 do not contain h264_amf.
encoding_capabilities._encoder_row_codec uses the duplicated name map exactly when family is absent or unrecognized.
A no-write reproduction with [{'encoder_name':'h264_amf','available':True}] returned capability-row codecs=[], backends=['amf','copy']; wizard-name codecs=['h264'], backends=['amf','copy'].

Validating a supported PresetV2 legacy codec h264_amf with codecFamily=h264 and encoderBackend=auto against those row facts produced video.codecFamily: Video codec 'h264' is not advertised by encoder capabilities.
The existing descriptor-row test supplies explicit family for every available encoder and therefore cannot exercise this fallback omission.
affected_flows: AMF H.264 configuration on descriptors with incomplete/legacy family metadata
existing_safeguards: Option policy and settings metadata explicitly allow h264_amf.
Descriptor rows with family=h264 bypass the faulty name fallback.
Preset capability tests cover unavailable codecs/backends and several descriptor rows.
safeguard_gap: No parity test covers every allowed encoder name across wizard and descriptor-row derivation, and no test removes/invalidates the descriptor family to exercise the fallback map.
tests_present: tests/python/core/contract/test_preset_policy_contract.py covers capability validation and derivation from descriptor rows.
tests/python/desktop/test_service_config_option_policy.py and test_service_config_validation.py assert h264_amf is an accepted option.
tests_missing: Parameterized parity test over every accepted encoder name across all capability derivation entry points.
Descriptor-row fallback test for h264_amf with missing, blank, and unknown family fields.
Settings-policy test proving an available h264_amf row permits an H.264 preset.
recommended_remediation: Replace the three maps with one canonical encoder descriptor/name registry used by wizard discovery, capability-row fallback, option policy, and metadata. As the minimal correction, add h264_amf to encoding_capabilities._ENCODER_CODECS_BY_NAME, then add exhaustive parity and missing-family fallback tests.
remediation_risk: Low-to-medium: the immediate mapping addition is narrow, but consolidating capability policy can affect CPU/GPU routing labels and settings validation. Do not change FFmpeg command generation as part of this fix.
validation_rung: Targeted preset-policy contract, settings capability, option-policy, and wizard tests plus a synthetic descriptor matrix for every supported encoder name. No real-media validation is required unless encoder routing or FFmpeg command generation is also changed.
prior_audit_relationship: No current finding ledger mentioned h264_amf or encoding_capabilities.py; this is a new current-hash finding.

title: Handler policy consumes an ungoverned desktop mirror of the canonical API contract
observed_behavior: The public/canonical route contract is assembled from mediapipeline.contracts, while handler_policy builds security-sensitive journal-exclusion decisions from a separate mediapipeline.desktop.api.contract_command tree. The two operation files have already diverged on the clean /api/rename/preview row: the canonical row requires preview_fingerprint and describes its freshness contract, while the desktop mirror omits required_response_fields and retains older purpose text. Existing parity coverage compares only the maintenance tuple.
expected_invariant: There must be one authoritative route-metadata object for documentation, strict payload/response obligations, handler effect classification, and command-journal policy, or an exhaustive generated parity gate must prove all mirrors identical on every behavior-bearing field.
root_cause: The route-contract hierarchy was copied under contracts/api_routes_* and desktop/api/contract_* and both trees remain imported. Partial tests compare only one slice, so route additions and metadata edits can land in one tree without failing a repository gate.
failure_scenario: A maintainer correctly marks a new or changed canonical route journaled=false or effect=secret-transfer but misses the desktop mirror. The public contract and contract tests pass, while handler_policy still journals validation failures or route exceptions for secret-bearing payloads. Conversely, response obligations can disappear from the desktop view, as the current rename-preview drift demonstrates.
evidence: The canonical rename-preview row has required_response_fields=['preview_fingerprint']; the desktop mirror has no required_response_fields key. A structural no-write comparison reported exactly that canonical-only key on this clean route row.

handler_policy.py imports .contract_command, not mediapipeline.contracts.api_routes_command, and uses effect/journaled fields from that mirror to decide whether validation and exception failures are recorded.
The two full route hierarchies include several currently byte-identical file pairs, proving duplicated ownership, while operations and other slices can diverge independently.
test_api_command_contracts imports both trees but the explicit dual-tree loop covers only LOCAL_API_MAINTENANCE_COMMAND_ROUTE_CONTRACT; no exhaustive route/field parity assertion exists.
A distinct worker-14 finding on the canonical operations file demonstrates separate route-to-payload drift but does not cover this dual-authority root cause.
affected_flows: future route metadata changes across all command families
existing_safeguards: Handler-policy tests assert the current network secret-transfer routes are not journaled.
Strict payload models and route inventory checks cover route registration.
The canonical and desktop maintenance contract slices receive a focused parity-like assertion.
safeguard_gap: No test asserts identical method/path sets and behavior-bearing metadata across both complete trees, and handler policy does not consume the canonical contract it publishes elsewhere. Current rename drift proves the gap is active even though effect/journaled values on that specific row still match.
tests_present: tests/python/desktop/test_api_command_contracts.py covers route/payload registration, strict confirmations, secret-transfer journal behavior, and only maintenance-slice dual-tree inspection.
tests_missing: Exhaustive canonical-versus-desktop route dictionary parity across method, path, effect, journaled, confirmations, request keys, and response obligations.
Test proving handler_policy's metadata object is the same authoritative object exported by the public contract.
Negative fixture showing a one-tree secret-transfer change fails the gate.
recommended_remediation: Make handler_policy and desktop contract adapters import the canonical mediapipeline.contracts route metadata. Remove the mirrored implementation files after compatibility/package checks, or generate them from the canonical tree with an exact check. Until consolidation, add an exhaustive structural parity test over every route and every behavior-bearing field.
remediation_risk: Medium: route metadata drives strict command journaling and secret handling. Consolidation must preserve import compatibility and verify all strict-confirmation, command-journal, and route inventory behavior.
validation_rung: Targeted API contract, handler policy, strict JSON, command journal, secret-redaction, route inventory, and affected WebView contract tests. No real-media validation is required.
prior_audit_relationship: Worker-14 finding AUDIT-FIND-W14-001 reports a route-to-Pydantic mismatch on /api/rename/filter-cases in the canonical operations file. This finding is distinct: it identifies two simultaneously imported route-contract authorities and a current rename-preview divergence between them.
